prompt:
You normalize one contact record embedded in a short note. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly the keys name, phone, email, company, country. All keys must be present, with string or null values. No Markdown or other text.

Use only the record's label/value lines. Labels and line order vary; separators include colon, equals and tab. Trim every value and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Absent, empty and placeholder values are null: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD (whole-value, any case). Never guess or use notes, signatures, domains or legal suffixes as sources for missing fields. The country-from-phone exception below is the only override.

Assign by content before normalizing. The value containing @ is the email, irrespective of its label. The phone is the value made only of digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / with at least seven digits after removing any leading tel: and a trailing extension of the form ext. N, ext N, xN, #N or extension N. N denotes extension digits. Read country from its own line. If the name-line value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company-line value does not, swap these two before cleaning.

Name: split Last, First at the first comma and put First before Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, with or without a dot, in any case. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space- or hyphen-separated part. Keep Unicode letters and all diacritics; never transliterate.

Company: remove a trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, case-insensitively. The suffix list is AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: strip the mailto: prefix and surrounding angle brackets, then lowercase the entire address. Do not change spelling, add accents or rebuild the address from the person's name.

Country: return uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Accept English, Swedish and German country names and alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes in any case, plus aliases including UK and Great Britain → GB, Holland → NL, USA and U.S.A. → US, Türkiye → TR, Czech Republic → CZ.

Phone: return E.164, with + followed only by calling-code and national significant digits. Remove tel: and the extension. Ignoring an opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 marks an international phone. Replace 00 with +, remove (0) and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Keep the written calling code. If country is missing, infer it from this code only if it uniquely identifies a country: shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. If a supplied country disagrees with the code, keep the supplied country and the phone's written code. For a national phone, strip formatting separators, remove one leading trunk 0 and prepend + and the normalized record country's calling code; if country is missing, phone is null.

Worked example — input:
Name = VÉLDRISS, Mx. ORVI-MAËL
Phone = <mailto:O.VELDRRISS@FENQLUME.INVALID>
Email = tel:(+358) (0)41/836.2745 #53
Org = FENQLUME, Oyj
Country = TBD

Output:
{"name":"Orvi-Maël Véldriss","phone":"+358418362745","email":"o.veldrriss@fenqlume.invalid","company":"Fenqlume","country":"FI"}
